title: I Bought An Elves Frame Anonymously (again)

takeaways.text: After a problematic pre-production review sample, the creator bought a second frame anonymously in March 2023 through the Australian distributor; promised delivery of about 15 days stretched past three months, which Elves attributed to a factory move.

A mechanic and a carbon repairer found filler on the seat-tube top, rough resin in the bottom-bracket shell, uneven bearing-cup wall thickness, excess adhesive inside, and pitting in the lower headset bearing seat on the anonymously bought frame.

Steerer wall thickness measured about 2 mm on one fork; the repairer saw a mixed glass-fibre and carbon layer and readings suggesting delamination on the pre-production steerer, which a cut section did not settle conclusively.

Elves replied that its forks use a fibreglass inner steerer layer for reaming (changed from white to black) and that frames contain none; a senior engineer at another brand told the creator glass fibre is common for machined steerers and metal inserts.

disclosure: The creator presents the frame as an anonymous purchase and names the Falath Evo in the description; other commercial arrangements are not established.
summary: Assessment of a purchased Falath EVO frameset with a carbon specialist and mechanic. This is the 2023 EVO sample, not evidence for EVO+ or EXP revisions or every production frame.
